subject: Early Science & Sensory Learning
standard_explanation: Human sensory perception is mediated by five primary specialized sensory modalities: vision (photoreceptors in the eyes), audition (mechanoreceptors in the inner ear cochlea), olfaction (chemoreceptors in the nasal mucosa), gustation (taste buds on the lingual papillae), and somatosensation (tactile, thermoreceptive, and mechanoreceptive nerve endings in the skin).
simplified_explanation: We have five amazing superpowers to explore our world! 1. Eyes to see colorful butterflies. 2. Ears to hear birds singing. 3. Nose to smell sweet flowers. 4. Tongue to taste delicious strawberries. 5. Hands to touch and pet soft, fluffy puppies!
key_points: Eyes help us SEE shapes, colors, and the bright sun.
Ears help us HEAR music, laughter, and bell chimes.
Nose helps us SMELL flowers and fresh food baking.
Tongue helps us TASTE sweet fruits and yummy food.
Hands and skin help us TOUCH and feel soft, warm, or cold things.
examples: Looking at a rainbow with your eyes.
Listening to gentle raindrops with your ears.
Smelling sweet lavender flowers with your nose.
misconceptions: Misconception: We only feel touch with our fingers. Fact: Skin all over your body can feel warm sun or gentle breeze.
Misconception: You can taste food without smelling it. Fact: Smell and taste work together as team superpowers to taste food.

assessment_questions.question: Which body part do we use to see colorful rainbows?
assessment_questions.hint: They blink and let you look at books.

assessment_questions.question: Which superpower sense lets you smell a fragrant rose flower?
assessment_questions.hint: It sits right in the middle of your face.
